learning: Check max_error on the s-bend and slalom against 0.06 m, and oval steering_oscillation against 0.25. If oscillation exceeds 0.25, raise kd further or move sensor y to 0.03. Report per-track values.
notes: Adopts the Builder's narrower, shorter, lighter chassis on the validated ±0.08 m, 0.016 m array. Controller is unchanged except kd rises to 0.9 to damp the higher effective yaw gain from the narrower track.
rationale: Iteration 3 (±0.08 m span, 0.04 m spacing, 0.016 m footprint) removed line loss on the s-bend and slalom (0 events per run, down from 0.6 and 0.95), but every track still ends off_track at the 0.06 m max_error floor, with progress only 0.18 on the s-bend and 0.09 on the slalom. The robot stays on the tape but drifts past the limit, so the limit is now steering response, not sensing. Oval steering_oscillation was 0.16, well below 0.25, so the sensor lead does not need to change. The Builder's geometry narrows wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10 m, shortens body_length 0.16 to 0.12 m, and lightens mass 0.8 to 0.7 kg. Turn rate per PWM count scales with 1/wheel_track, so the narrower track gives about 1.2x more yaw per unit of turn, and lower mass reduces yaw inertia. The sensor array is unchanged, so I keep kp at 6 and ki at 0.05 as in iteration 3. I raise kd from 0.8 to 0.9 to damp the extra yaw response and hold base_speed at 1.5. Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom with rising progress. The main risk is oval steering_oscillation above 0.25, which would trigger the sensor y change next.
